settings.heading: Our lab reports
settings.lead: When a batch is tested, its laboratory report is published here with the batch number, so you can match it to your jar.

settings.heading: Find your batch
settings.note: Values are as printed on each laboratory report. ppm means parts per million.
settings.empty_text: Our laboratory reports will appear on this page as soon as they are ready. Questions in the meantime? Message us on WhatsApp.

settings.heading: What the numbers mean
settings.text:
Each report lists the batch number, the laboratory that tested it and the test date.

Fulvic acid is shown as a percentage. Heavy metals (lead, arsenic, mercury and cadmium) are shown in parts per million (ppm): lower is better.

settings.title: It dissolves fully
settings.text: Real resin dissolves in warm water or milk and turns it golden to reddish-brown, without gritty residue.

settings.title: It softens with warmth
settings.text: Resin turns soft and sticky when warmed in your hand and firms up again when cold.

settings.title: It is dark and glossy
settings.text: Resin is dark brown to black with a glossy, tar-like look. It is not a dry powder.

settings.title: It smells earthy
settings.text: Expect a strong, earthy smell and a bitter taste. A sweet or perfumed smell is a warning sign.

settings.heading: Four ways to check shilajit at home
settings.lead: Simple checks people commonly use to tell real resin from imitations.
settings.footnote: These checks are a guide only. They do not replace a lab report.
